name: Louisiana veterans: parish veterans service offices for claims help
description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from Louisiana Department of Veterans Affairs staff. Every parish is served by a department office.

constraints: Many parish offices are open only one to three days a week; check the days and call before you go.

name: Louisiana Answers: aging and disability information line
organization: Governor’s Office of Elderly Affairs, Aging and Disability Resource Centers
description: Louisiana’s Aging and Disability Resource Centers help older adults and adults with disabilities find long-term care options, prescription assistance and local services. The statewide information, referral and assistance line connects you to the center for your parish. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 877-340-9100, or choose a parish above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.
Give your parish so the call reaches the right center.

name: Medicare counseling (SHIIP) for Louisiana
organization: Louisiana Department of Insurance, Senior Health Insurance Information Program (SHIIP)
description: Free, confidential Medicare counseling from the Department of Insurance’s Senior Health Insurance Information Program and its partner counselors around the state: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help paying for Medicare. The department also calls it LaSHIP.
next_step: Call 800-259-5300 and ask for a SHIIP counselor, or use the department’s page to find help near you. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

name: Louisiana Long-Term Care Ombudsman and elder abuse reporting
organization: Governor’s Office of Elderly Affairs, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
description: Independent advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, through seven regional programs and the state office.
next_step: Call the state ombudsman office at 866-632-0922, or choose a parish above for its regional ombudsman. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of someone 60 or older, call Elderly Protective Services at 833-577-6532 (after hours: 844-945-2377). For adults 18 to 59, call Adult Protective Services at 800-898-4910. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free legal help for Louisiana veterans and older adults
organization: Southeast Louisiana Legal Services; Acadiana Legal Service Corporation
description: Louisiana’s legal aid programs give free civil legal help to people with low incomes. Southeast Louisiana Legal Services serves 22 parishes in the southeast and helps veterans with discharge upgrades, VA benefits and VA overpayments. Acadiana Legal Service Corporation serves 42 parishes in north, central and southwest Louisiana.
next_step: In southeast Louisiana, call Southeast Louisiana Legal Services at 844-244-7871 or apply online. Elsewhere, call Acadiana Legal Service Corporation at 866-275-2572. The Louisiana State Bar Association’s Find Legal Help portal lists other free and reduced-fee options.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income, case type and parish.
Neither program handles criminal cases.

name: VA health care systems serving Louisiana
description: Louisiana veterans are served mainly by the Southeast Louisiana Veterans Health Care System (New Orleans VA Medical Center, 2400 Canal Street; 800-935-8387), the Alexandria VA Health Care System (2495 Shreveport Highway, Pineville; 318-473-0010) and the Overton Brooks VA Medical Center in Shreveport (510 East Stoner Avenue; 318-990-5547), with clinics across the state.
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask your parish veterans service office for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

name: New Horizons Independent Living Center (Shreveport, Monroe, Alexandria)
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your parish and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Main office: 1701 North Market Street, Shreveport, LA 71107; toll-free 877-219-7327.
Branch offices: Monroe, 1401 Hudson Lane, Suite 200 (318-323-4374, toll-free 800-428-5505); Alexandria, 3717 Government Street, Suite 7 (318-484-3596, toll-free 888-361-3596).
The card links to the national directory because no secure (https) website address for this center appears in the sources read.

organization: Volunteers of America Southeast Louisiana, Inc.
